## The loss curve attains its minimum at K = 7 = K_true in BOTH folds, descends monotonically
## from K=4 to K=7 and rises monotonically from K=7 to K=10. The silhouette holds ~0.996
## through K=7 and drops sharply at K=8 (0.826, 0.851) in both folds. Two independent
## signals place the elbow at K_true.
## ---- WHY CRITERION 2 FAILED ANYWAY, AND WHY THAT IS A DEFECT IN THE CRITERION ----
## Criterion 2 inspects only K_true and K_max. Its stated rationale in the pre-registration
## is: "Both ends sitting on the irreducible Poisson floor means no selector can work,
## whatever its rule, because there is no signal left to select on."
## That rationale is falsified by this run's own data. There IS signal: the curve spans
## 1.137 -> 1.016 (outer_0) and 1.166 -> 1.010 (outer_1) across the grid, and criterion 1
## resolves the K_true -> K_max rise at t = 26.8. The criterion measured the wrong span. It
## looked only at the overfit side of the minimum, where the curve is by construction nearly
## flat, and never at the underfit side, where this benchmark's dynamic range actually lives.
## It passed at SMOKE by an accident of that grid's shape: K_max = 4 there sat on the
## underfit side of a K_true = 3 curve, so "K_max" happened to name a high-error point.
## At this grid K_max = 10 names a low-error point. The same rule therefore tests a
## different thing at the two tiers. That is a mis-specification, not a property of cNMF.
## THIS DOES NOT LICENSE OVERRIDING THE VERDICT. The pre-registration states plainly that
## "changing the criteria above" is not permitted, and a criterion rewritten by the person
## who has just seen it fail is worth nothing regardless of how sound the argument is. The
## recorded verdict for this run is NO-GO.
## What the defect licenses instead is a SEPARATE, newly pre-registered criterion, written
## with the explicit acknowledgement that it postdates this data, and evaluated on a FRESH
## run at a different seed. A criterion tested on the data that motivated it has no
## evidential force. See DECISIONS.md D012.
## ---- INCIDENTAL: thin identity-program carriers ----
## n_training_carriers_per_identity_program = [12, 3, 3, 4, 1] (outer_0), [12, 3, 5, 4, 3] (outer_1).
## One identity program has a SINGLE training carrier donor in outer_0. Recorded here because
## it bears directly on feature A: a program carried by one donor cannot be learned in a way
## that generalises across donors, and donor-blocked evaluation is the thing that would
## expose that. Not acted on in this run.
